measured_in: HELM, after the merge of yard-an-audit-log-deleted-by-its-own-cleanup. Two full pre-push runs, 664s and 820s, both 7069/2758 exactly.

also_measured.the_fourth_run: 6925/2714, the only run of six that differed, and the only one that overlapped a YARD writing into the shared data overlay. Cost of one concurrent writer, measured once: +4 children, +1 test.

note: Shrink-only, and BOTH numbers are measured in HELM rather than derived. THE 2026-09-09 MOVE, 6930/2715 -> 7078/2760, IS THE SUITE GROWING AND NOT THE GATE BEING RELAXED, and the distinction is the only thing that makes the move legitimate. Five commits between 0f348c2 and the merge of yard-an-audit-log-deleted-by-its-own-cleanup added roughly forty-five test functions that spawn a child, and the gate's own offender report names one of them from 19faaaa: `20x tests/test_a_probe_that_asked_whether_it_was_inside_any_repository.py::test_a_second_run_on_the_same_target_is_a_no_op -> git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. Two full pre-push runs in HELM on 2026-09-09 gave 7069/2758 EXACTLY, at 664s and 820s, so this is not the pre-4e535b1 flap returning: after the wire fix the number stopped moving with load, and it did not move here either. WHAT WAS REJECTED, recorded so it is not re-argued: freezing at the observed values with no margin (tried on 2026-09-06, red on the very next run, because the margin is for concurrency and not for noise); and leaving the gate red until the spawn count is reduced, which is the RIGHT fix and is deferred rather than done. THE REDUCTION WORK IS OUTSTANDING AND THIS ENTRY DOES NOT DISCHARGE IT. The largest single offender is 224 spawns of `uname -p` attributed to no test, whose caller is NOT IDENTIFIED as of 2026-09-09: the only path in CPython that spawns it is `platform.processor()`, `platform.uname()` with `.release` and `.machine` accessed spawns nothing (measured with a shim on PATH the same day), and telethon's `TelegramClient.__init__` was wrongly suspected on the strength of a `platform.uname()` call that cannot reach it. Next after that: 160 spawns from test_a_runaway_loop_guard_that_lost_the_events_it_counted. THE HEADROOM IS FOR CONCURRENCY, NOT FOR NOISE, and that distinction was paid for. The margin here is +9 children and +2 tests over the observed figure, the same shape 6930/2715 carried over 6921/2713: sized to the one measured perturbation (+4 children, +1 test per concurrent overlay writer) and doubled for two. THE OLD 6100 WAS NOT MERELY STALE: it was computed from runs that each silently lost one to three xdist workers, so it sat below the honest figure by construction. An unencodable surrogate escape in a sample spawn killed `workerfinished`, the whole `workeroutput` was dropped, and the run stayed green with one `node down:` line as its only trace (fixed in 4e535b1 by sanitising at the wire; evidence in outputs/operations/overlay-gate-2026-09-06/). Before that fix the spread over one unchanged tree was 5% on children and 6% on distinct tests; after it, three HELM runs across a hundredfold change in machine load gave 2713 distinct tests every single time. THE COUNT REMAINS CLONE-DEPENDENT: 50 tests skip in a worktree (MAIN_CLONE_SKIP, 'no data overlay on this clone'), measured on 2026-09-06 as 6921 in HELM against 6814 in a yard on the identical commit, so never ratchet either number down from a figure a worktree reported. If this gate flaps again, the first thing to check is not the metric: assert that every worker delivered (`sum sent == sum received`) and grep the output for `node down`, because a green run is not evidence that every worker reported.
